records.segregation: disease linked to a 4-Mb region at 2p13
quotes: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution

notes.statement: Münch et al. (2004) screened the DCTN1 and DNCHC1 genes in 250 patients with ALS and 150 controls. They found heterozygous DCTN1 missense mutations in 1 apparently sporadic ALS case (T1249I), 1 individual with familial ALS (M571T), and 2 patients with familial ALS plus 2 unaffected relatives in the same kindred (R785W). They suggested that DCTN1 variants may be a genomic risk factor for ALS.
quotes: Heterozygous missense mutations of the DCTN1 gene were detected in one apparently sporadic case of ALS (T1249I), one individual with familial ALS (M571T), two patients with familial ALS, and two unaffected relatives in the same kindred (R785W).
The allelic variants of the DCTN1 gene may represent a previously unknown genomic risk factor for ALS.

notes.statement: Puls et al. (2003) showed linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a 4-Mb region on chromosome 2p13.
quotes: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.

notes.statement: Puls et al. (2003) found a single base-pair change in the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin that resulted in an amino acid substitution. They predicted that it would distort the folding of the microtubule-binding domain of dynactin.
quotes: showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution that is predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain

notes.statement: In binding assays, Puls et al. (2003) found that the mutant dynactin protein bound less to microtubules. They concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated axonal transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
quotes: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.
Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
